label: H.R. 7332

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Whale CHARTS Act of 2026 amends the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 to establish and expand programs focused on mapping, surveying, monitoring, and mitigating risks to migratory whales and other large cetaceans. The legislation requires the production of distribution maps, understudied species surveys, a competitive grant program managed through the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation for detection technologies, and periodic reporting to Congress.

affected_groups.effect: The Under Secretary and relevant federal agencies must design distribution maps, conduct surveys, administer grants, coordinate with the Coast Guard, and submit periodic reports to Congress.
Eligible entities can participate in consultations regarding mapping priorities and apply for competitive grants related to whale monitoring and detection technologies.
affected_groups.group: State, local, and Tribal governments and research institutions

affected_groups.effect: Commercial or recreational vessels may integrate electronic and machine-readable distribution maps into on-board navigation systems, and maritime sectors may receive grants to develop detection tools.

key_provisions: Directs the Under Secretary, in consultation with the Marine Mammal Commission, to produce high-accuracy current and predictive distribution maps for migratory whales in U.S. waters.
Requires the Under Secretary to conduct surveys specific to understudied stocks, populations, or species of migratory whales to estimate abundance and distribution.
Establishes a competitive grant program administered by the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation to fund detection technologies, research, and collaborative coexistence approaches.

Authorizes specific appropriations for fiscal years 2026 through 2030, including $2 million annually for distribution mapping, $1 million annually for understudied surveys, $5 million annually for the mitigation subprogram, and $10 million for the grant program.
Mandates regular reports to Congress and the public regarding mapping activities, knowledge gaps, and grant project results every three years following an initial two-year report.
Requires the Secretary to consider newly produced distribution maps when preparing, publishing, or reviewing marine mammal stock assessments.
missing_information: The text does not specify exact implementation details or performance benchmarks beyond broad authorizations and reporting timelines.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Whale CHARTS Act of 2026 amends the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 to establish and expand programs focused on mapping, surveying, monitoring, and mitigating risks to migratory whales and other large cetaceans. The legislation requires the production of distribution maps, understudied species surveys, a competitive grant program managed through the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation for detection technologies, and periodic reporting to Congress.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates federal programs and authorizes funding to track and protect migratory whales from vessel strikes and disturbances in U.S. waters. It implements systematic mapping, targeted surveys, and technology grants across federal, state, and maritime stakeholder groups.
